question: Why should a test set remain separate from model training and tuning?
options: To estimate performance on data not used to fit or select the model
To increase the number of training labels automatically
To guarantee the model will never make errors
To replace validation during model selection
correctAnswer: To estimate performance on data not used to fit or select the model
explanation: A held-out test set provides a less biased estimate of generalization when it is not repeatedly used to tune model choices.

question: For a rare disease screening model, why might recall be an important metric?
options: It measures the fraction of actual positive cases that are found
It measures the fraction of all predictions that are correct
It measures the number of input features
correctAnswer: It measures the fraction of actual positive cases that are found
explanation: Recall is true positives divided by all actual positives. Missing a positive case can be costly in screening, though precision and other trade-offs must also be considered.

question: What is data leakage in a machine-learning workflow?
options: Using information during training that would not be available at prediction time
Encoding a categorical feature using training data
Splitting records into training and test sets
correctAnswer: Using information during training that would not be available at prediction time
explanation: Leakage gives the model access to target-related or future information unavailable in real use, producing overly optimistic evaluation.

question: What does a 95% confidence level mean for a procedure used repeatedly?
options: About 95% of intervals produced by the procedure would contain the fixed parameter
There is a 95% probability that this specific computed interval contains the parameter
95% of observations lie inside every confidence interval
The null hypothesis has a 95% probability of being true
correctAnswer: About 95% of intervals produced by the procedure would contain the fixed parameter
explanation: In the frequentist interpretation, the confidence level describes the long-run coverage of the interval-generating procedure under its assumptions.
